output.title: Letter to Governor-General Willem Arnold Alting regarding English Ship Atlas
output.abstract: Official VOC correspondence addressed to Governor-General Willem Arnold Alting in Batavia concerning the Dutch East India Company's dealings with an English vessel named the Atlas. The document appears to be a duplicate letter (Duplicaet) documenting the dispatch of the English ship, likely related to commercial or diplomatic matters between the VOC and English maritime interests in the East Indies during the 18th century.

output.title: Financial Management and Currency Arrangements for Ceylon, 1785
output.abstract: VOC correspondence addressing financial demands from Ceylon and measures to meet them. Discusses challenges in obtaining private credit due to limited resources among local inhabitants, introduction of paper money, copper coinage expansion, and interest rate increases to 9%. Details coordination between chambers (Rotterdam, Amsterdam, Cape) for fund distribution and requests for sovereign financial support to address currency shortages and commercial difficulties.

output.title: VOC Emergency Measures and Distribution of Indian and Cape Goods
output.abstract: This document discusses the VOC's desperate financial situation and emergency measures undertaken to address critical shortages. The text details plans for the Commissioners to distribute Indian and Cape goods among the respective chambers in June, contingent upon resolution from the sovereign authority. It emphasizes the urgent need for relief supplies and instructs the chambers to remit allocated funds to India and the Cape at the earliest opportunity.

output.title: Extract from VOC Letter to Governor-General, November 1784
output.abstract: Extract from correspondence dated 18 November 1784 from the Amsterdam chamber to the Governor-General and Council in Batavia. Reports on receipt of letters from May and August 1784. Describes complications with mail delivery: documents sent from Cape of Good Hope aboard the company vessel Zwaluw were forced to land at Padang due to the ship's poor condition and were sold as unrecoverable. Consequently, letters and papers were rerouted overland via Spain to Amsterdam.

output.title: Bengal Rice Supply Contract and Sjankoosen Diving Rights, Ceylon 1780-1784
output.abstract: VOC correspondence regarding a proposal to supply 800-1000 lasts of Bengali coastal rice annually to Ceylon at 4 rixdollars per 150-pound sack. The Company suspended sjankoosen (pearl diving) farming to pursue rice procurement directly. Outstanding payment issues and disputes over compensation involving merchant Blinne and former director Ross's estate are discussed, with references to peace treaty negotiations and recovery of assets lost during the capture of Trincomalee.

output.title: Linen Pacht Compensation and Arrears Settlement, Colombo 1782
output.abstract: VOC resolution regarding compensation for a linen (lijwaad) pacht farmer in Colombo who suffered losses during his lease period. The farmer submitted sworn accounts detailing reduced linen imports due to wartime disruptions (war news received June 1781). VOC officials approved a reduced payment of 7,250.36¾ rixdollars instead of the full 16,080 rixdollars owed, acknowledging accumulated arrears from previous years (1776-1780) and the paucity of linen deliveries during his tenure.

output.title: Compensation of Secretaries' Widows and Recovery of Outstanding Twintigste Penny (1782)
output.abstract: VOC administrative resolution addressing compensation for widows of secretaries Lebeck who served in Pale, following orders from April 1782. Documents efforts to recover outstanding twintigste penny (twentieth penny tax) from fiscal years 1775-1776, noting gross negligence in delayed collection. Discusses accountability measures and directives to ensure proper settlement of arrears and compensation to affected parties.

output.title: Fortification Works at Trincomalee and Defense Concerns, 1782
output.abstract: VOC correspondence regarding fortification construction at Trincomalee under Knight Des Roijs, addressing concerns raised in secret missives of April and June 1782. Documents discuss incomplete defensive works, inadequate land-side fortifications, and the fort's vulnerability when surrendered to enemy forces. Evaluates the state of preparedness and construction management during this critical period.

output.title: VOC Response to Loss of Ships and Frigates During Anglo-Dutch War, 1781
output.abstract: VOC administrative document discussing the loss of ships and their cargoes during wartime conflict with the English, circa December 1781. References the disappearance of frigates between 5-24 December 1781 and orders issued to Trincomalee regarding two chaloupes (small vessels). Examines whether timely precautions could have prevented losses and whether burning ships was preferable to allowing English capture. Includes correspondence from February 12 regarding ministerial directives to Trincomalee.

output.title: Investigation of Smuggling Allegations and Captain Jansen's Death
output.abstract: VOC document examining suspected smuggling involving Captain Jansen and an English vessel anchored in Paalsche Bay. The investigation was discontinued following Jansen's death, preventing proper interrogation. The document discusses how accusations were potentially used to deflect blame, and notes that the Warehouse Master's involvement actually increased rather than diminished suspicions against him.

output.title: Resolution of 11 October: Cargo Transfer and Ship Movements to Kutch and Porca
output.abstract: VOC resolution documenting the unloading of goods from the ship de Bodt onto the Spaarenrijk at Pale, with subsequent dispatch to Kutch (Koetsjim) on 20 November to procure pepper and rice. Reports delayed arrival of vessels and confirms the Spaarenrijk's return voyage from Porca to Ceylon on 1 December, following pepper collection operations coordinated with local ministers.

output.title: Reassignment of Ship Stavenisse to Amsterdam Chamber and Cargo Instructions
output.abstract: VOC administrative decision from 24 December redirecting the ship Stavenisse from Zeeland Chamber to Amsterdam Chamber for loading. The reassignment was necessitated by the ship's apparent failure to reach Ceylon and the shortage of pepper and saltpeter supplies needed to load two return vessels. Instructions issued to Palembang officials regarding ballast and cargo arrangements for the Stavenisse.

output.title: Arrival and Disposition of Ships Stavenisse and Middelwijk at Batavia
output.abstract: VOC administrative record documenting the arrival and cargo handling of the return ships Stavenisse and Middelwijk at Batavia in October-November. The Stavenisse, consigned to Amsterdam chamber, arrived October 10 after rapid passage from the Netherlands and was subsequently dispatched to Coetsjiem and Gale with rice, pepper, and naval supplies. The Middelwijk arrived October 19 with partial cargo unloaded at Batavia. Includes disposition orders and resolutions from November-December regarding cargo distribution.

output.title: Horse Inventory and Coarse Linen Trade Regulations at Colombo
output.abstract: VOC administrative record documenting horse stocks on Delft Island (228 animals including Persian stallions, local mares, and foals) with maintenance costs of ƒ817.5.8, and concurrent regulations from March-July regarding coarse linen (lijwaeten) procurement on the Madura coast. Includes price adjustments and trade restrictions to optimize company collections and comptoir operations.

output.title: Pearl Fishery Leasing and Agreement with the Count of Bijland, Ceylon
output.abstract: VOC administrative document concerning the leasing of pearl fisheries (duijkerij) along the Ceylon coast and at Tutucorijn. Details negotiations with the Count of Bijland regarding contract terms and compensation arrangements. Records valuation disputes (3600 rixdollars deemed below standard value) and September 3rd resolution to maintain fishery operations under company account to fulfill contractual obligations from June 24-30 agreements.

output.title: VOC Pricing and Administration of Cinnamon Trade at Calicut and Ceylon, 1786
output.abstract: Administrative record documenting VOC decisions regarding cinnamon (sjankos) pricing and procurement at Calicut (Kalpettij) and Ceylon trading posts. Details include wage adjustments for cinnamon workers (rd:s 16:32), quantity thresholds, and inspection reports by appointed commissioners including Dessave De Bock. References October 22 and December 29 resolutions, and August 26 visitation of English trading banks along Ceylon coast.

output.title: Pearl Oyster Inspection Report: Tuticorin and Madura Banks
output.abstract: VOC report documenting inspection visits to pearl oyster beds at Tuticorin and Madura (Madras coast), conducted by Captain Commandant of Calicut and subordinate merchants. Despite high expectations, inspections yielded minimal and immature pearl oysters. Resolution of 29 December records findings. Additional inspection of Madura coast pearl banks authorized following petition by Nabab Machmiet Alichan, with results to be reported separately.

output.title: Purchase of Trade Goods and Provisions, 1710
output.abstract: VOC procurement record documenting the purchase of essential supplies and trade goods during 1710. Notable acquisition includes 6,000 sacks of Bengali rice (150 lb each) at six rixdollars per sack from English ship Stasting from Bengal. Additional purchases of Dutch maritime supplies—rope, sailcloth, sail yarn, pitch, tar, and hemp—were made to meet urgent needs of the Dutch squadron. Multiple resolutions from January through December authorize these acquisitions.

output.title: VOC Spice and Dutch Merchandise Inventory with Purchase and Sale Prices
output.abstract: VOC trading ledger documenting inventory valuations for Eastern spices (cloves, mace, nutmeg, cinnamon) and Dutch merchandise including textiles, metalwork, glassware, and equipment. Records purchase prices (Inkoops), sale prices (Verkoops), and profit margins (Winst) in guilders and stuivers, with quantities measured in pounds and pieces. Demonstrates VOC's dual trading operations in Asian spices and European goods distribution.

output.title: VOC Cargo Inventory and Financial Account: Goods for Transport and Regional Distribution
output.abstract: This VOC accounting document records a comprehensive inventory of goods designated for transport and distribution to various colonial markets, particularly Coromandel and Ceylon. Items catalogued include textiles (pintams, calicuts, silk cloths), spices (pepper, cloves), provisions (rice, salt, coffee, sugar), medicinal compounds, and naval supplies. The document details departmental allocations (ship's carpentry, armory, dispensary) with corresponding financial valuations in guilders. Purchase and sales profit calculations are provided, indicating this served as both inventory control and commercial accounting for VOC operations.

output.title: VOC Spice Sales Pricing and Domain Revenue Report, 1784-1785
output.abstract: VOC administrative document detailing spice pricing resolutions from July 1784 and June 1785, establishing nutmeg prices at 100 rixdollars and mace at 150 stuivers per unit. Reports accounting discrepancies in clove sales calculations by bookkeeper Rakel. Documents domain revenues for fiscal year 1785-1786 totaling ƒ397,429.4, an increase of ƒ113,547.9.8 from the previous year. Addresses salt transport restrictions to upland regions and the resulting impact on Putelang lease auctions.

output.title: VOC Domain Leases and Pacter Concessions, August-September 1699
output.abstract: Record of public auctions for VOC domains in Jaffna and Mannar (26-27 August 1699) and linen leases in Colombo, Gale, and Kalpettij (3 September, 20,000 rixdollars). Documents preferential bidding rights granted to previous bidders when general lease prices exceeded their offers, and relief allowances granted to salt pan and cloth trade pacters due to losses from salt transport prohibitions and other commercial restrictions.

output.title: Pagoda Mint Output and Gold Shipment Records, Colombo 1784-1785
output.abstract: VOC administrative record documenting gold coinage production at the Pagoda Mint in Colombo from September 1784 to August 1785, totaling 101,759 pagodas from 1,413 marks of fine gold. Details shipment via the Trois Frères to the Cape of Good Hope, then by frigate Waaksaemheid to Galle and overland to Colombo. Lists individual gold bars (bhaar goud) with specifications, weights, and fineness ratings, representing precious metal transfers for the Zeeland chamber.

output.title: Gold Ingot Inventory and Valuation Records from VOC Ships Triton and Stavenisse
output.abstract: VOC accounting document recording detailed inventories of gold ingots (bhaaren goud) transported from Batavia and Zeeland to the Dutch East Indies. Lists 54 ingots from ship Triton and 15 ingots from ship Stavenisse, each individually numbered and assessed with weight measurements in karats and corresponding monetary values. Includes systematic pricing records and transport notations, reflecting VOC's precious metals management and commercial accounting practices in the early 18th century.

output.title: VOC Mint Records: Gold and Copper Assay Accounts and Coinage Transactions
output.abstract: VOC financial ledger documenting precious metal assaying and minting operations, including gold and Japanese copper refinement, pagoda coinage production, and associated costs. Records detail multiple minting batches with weight calculations in marks and ounces, assay deductions, labor costs for smiths and smelters, and final valuations in guilders. Entries reference fiscal oversight and transfers to the main cash treasury.

output.title: VOC Mint Operations: Gold and Silver Coinage Accounts and Transfers
output.abstract: Financial record documenting VOC mint (munterij) operations, including detailed accounts of gold coinage production across five minting batches with precise weight calculations in marks and fineness measurements. Records total receipts of ƒ408,595.7.1, deductions for pagoda conversions, and profit calculations. Notes the temporary closure of the Fanuis mint and decisions regarding worn silver items scheduled for reminting, with transfers to Tutukorin authorized by resolutions from April and November.

output.title: Commission for Assessment of Colombo Fortification Works
output.abstract: Report on a commission appointed March 3, 1760, to inspect and assess the fortification works at Colombo and recommend necessary improvements, following the model of similar inspections at Pale. The work has been delayed due to Major Paravicini's absence in Trincomalee. The document discusses the ship Stavenisse's potential delay in departure and promises a preliminary report for submission to the Directors and High Authorities.

output.title: Fortification Maintenance Protocols and Lieutenant Lawe's Accountability
output.abstract: VOC administrative directive concerning the continuous maintenance and fortification of three strategic defensive positions. Lieutenant Lawe, serving as engineer, is required to submit annual oaths affirming faithful treatment of coolies, laborers, and craftsmen under his department. The document emphasizes strict disciplinary measures for any dereliction of duty, with no leniency permitted. Work must proceed systematically to achieve the fortifications' defensive readiness.

output.title: Petition for Lieutenant Lowe's Salary and Carpentry Expenditure Report
output.abstract: A VOC administrative document petitioning for an annual salary increase of 1800 rixdollars (150 rixdollars monthly) for Lieutenant Lowe, arguing that adequate compensation prevents servants from breaching their oaths. The petition includes detailed carpentry and repair expenditures totaling ƒ56,898:10:— across multiple locations: Colombo (ƒ64,822:5:8), Jaffnapatnam (ƒ2,160:4:—), Mannaar (ƒ909:13:8), Galle (ƒ11,558:4:8), and Matara (ƒ395:14:2), emphasizing the Company's obligation to support loyal employees adequately.

output.title: Administrative Reconciliation Reports: Apothecary, Workshops, and Warehouses (1784)
output.abstract: VOC administrative reconciliation document detailing monthly apothecary reports on medicinal preparations and warehouse audits conducted in Colombo and Jaffnapatnam during August 1784. Records verification of workshop and iron magazine inventories, material house transfers, and ammunition warehouse accounts, with all findings approved and reconciled against official orders and negotiation books.

output.title: VOC Account Settlements and Administrative Dispositions, 1784-1785
output.abstract: VOC administrative document addressing account settlements and resolutions for multiple trading posts. Details dispositions regarding agent Geeke's accounts, negotiations at Pale (Colombo) warehouse findings from August 1784, and agent Zeeke's Tranquebar accounts (August 1784-January 1785). Documents dismissal of agent Peeke from Tranquebar in January 1785 pending final accounting and resolution of discrepancies with Captain Lieutenant De Bellon's records from the Coromandel coast. References correspondence with first visitor Berghuijs.

output.title: General Expenses and Profits Account, Fiscal Year 1784/5
output.abstract: VOC financial statement comparing general expenses and profits for fiscal year 1784/5 with previous year 1782/3. Documents total profits of ƒ643,770 in Dutch currency against expenses of ƒ1,503,564. Includes audit reports of payroll books from Colombo, Jaffnapatnam, and Pondicherry, verification of deed books and military rosters. Shows increased expenses of ƒ759,001 compared to prior year, with total assets in cash, merchandise, provisions, and equipment valued at ƒ6,126,694 as of August 1785.

output.title: Inspection of Supply Requisitions and Provisional Accounting Records from Ceylon and Nagapatnam
output.abstract: VOC administrative document detailing inspection of supply requisitions (eijsch van benodigheden) and provisional accounting procedures for Ceylon and Nagapatnam stations. References resolutions from February, March, and May regarding bookkeepers and medical personnel transferred from Nagapatnam. Addresses discrepancies between expenditure specifications and payment authorizations, with directives for handling minor accounting items.

output.title: VOC Inventory of Spices, Textiles, and Military Supplies (1786)
output.abstract: A detailed VOC warehouse inventory from January 1786 documenting quantities of colonial commodities including spices (cloves, nutmeg, mace), sugar, copper, Japanese copper ingots, tin, textiles (nanking linen), ceramics, rice, wax candles, arrak, gunpowder supplies, and military equipment. The document records stock levels across multiple storage locations including the dispensary, armory, and trade warehouse, reflecting the Company's extensive Asian trade operations and supply chain management.

output.title: VOC Supply Inventory: Timber, Medicines, and Smithy Materials
output.abstract: VOC warehouse inventory document detailing provisions for multiple workshops and departments. Lists medicinal substances (radix China, lignum Sassafras, oils, balms), timber materials for shipyards and carpentry shops with specific dimensions, and smithy supplies including Venetian borax and iron stock. Organized by department (timber yards, pharmacy, smiths and coopers), with quantities in pounds and pieces. Includes five-year consumption projections for provisioning purposes.

output.title: VOC Supply Inventory and Financial Records for Colonial Residencies, 1782
output.abstract: VOC administrative document detailing annual supply requisitions and financial accounts across multiple South Asian residencies including Colombo, Jaffna, Mannaar, Galle, Madura, Tuticorin, Batticaloa, and Kalpettij. Records enumerate timber supplies (large and small planks) allocated to shipyards, carpentry workshops, and gun carriage makers, alongside monetary accounts in guilders and commodity stocks (rice, coconut oil). Document reflects VOC's logistical organization and resource distribution across colonial settlements circa 1782.

output.title: Justice Council Complaint Against Orphanage Trustees and Enforcement Procedures
output.abstract: This document addresses a formal complaint by the Justice Council regarding orphanage trustees (weesmeesters) who failed to comply with council rulings and sought to appeal directly to higher authority. The text clarifies jurisdictional authority, establishing that orphan chambers must submit to the Justice Council's decisions and that enforcement measures (contrainte) may be applied against non-compliant trustees without exception.

output.title: Educational Institution Assessment and Teacher Quality Standards
output.abstract: VOC administrative correspondence addressing concerns about an educational establishment (likely a seminary or training institution) established with good intentions. The document references resolutions from April 15 and September 6, noting that recent graduates sent to the Netherlands had to return to lower classes. It discusses the need for better-qualified instructors and suggests that the Seminarium should focus on producing catechism masters and indigenous schoolmasters to justify the Company's substantial financial investment in the institution.

output.title: Jaffena Orphan Masters' Request for Welfare Support of European Widows and Orphans
output.abstract: The Jaffena (Jaffna) orphan masters petition for approval to use surplus interest from their chamber's funds to support European-descended widows and orphans in their jurisdiction. The VOC approves their proposal on May 7, 1784, authorizing limited distributions from accumulated rents (1117 rixdollars) without depleting capital, designating funds for compensation of losses affecting orphans' estates.

output.title: Diaconate Capital and Leper House Fund Accounts, Ceylon
output.abstract: VOC financial record detailing the Diaconate capital totaling ƒ126,161:14:6¼ distributed across Ceylon settlements: Colombo, Jaffna, Manaar, Gale, Mature, and Kalpettij. Documents repairs to the deteriorating Leper House (Leproosen huijs) authorized September 13, costing rixdollars 1709:14:½, and the Leper Fund balance of ƒ31,735:17½ as of August. References administrative resolutions and subsidiary account statements.

output.title: Pearl Fishery Disputes with Tuticorin and Nabab Negotiations
output.abstract: VOC correspondence regarding pearl bank inspections at Tuticorin and diplomatic negotiations with the Nabab over pearl fishery rights. Documents include letters exchanged between the Nabab, VOC leadership (Mekern), and the Governor, along with resolutions from September-December addressing disputes. English physician Dr. Dot was commissioned to mediate discussions on behalf of the Nabab concerning pearl fishing operations.

output.title: Renewal and Issuance of Don and Modliaar Titles at Jaffna, 1760
output.abstract: VOC administrative directive concerning the renewal and issuance of honorary titles (Don and Modliaar) at Jaffna. Holders of these titles since 1760 must renew their certificates within six weeks at a cost of 12.5 rixdollars. New applicants may also obtain titles for up to 25 rixdollars. The regulation clarifies that title acquisition is voluntary and poses no operational burden to the Company.

output.title: Appointment of Thomas Nagel as Land Surveyor and Administrator of Jaffnapatnam
output.abstract: Document concerning the appointment of artillery lieutenant and sworn land surveyor Thomas Nagel to direct administration of Jaffnapatnam territories under VOC control. Nagel is credited with designing the initial plan to bring these lands under Company authority and successfully suppressing a dangerous mutiny. His sixteen years of service as surveyor provided extensive territorial knowledge, and his character is deemed suitable for governing the Ceylorese lands effectively.

output.title: Negotiation with French Governor Coutancheau regarding supply of goods and ammunition
output.abstract: Record of negotiations between VOC officials and the French Governor Coutancheau at Pondicherry concerning the supply of deficient goods and ammunition. The French governor expressed willingness to provide necessary supplies but declined to establish fixed prices, instead proposing to deliver goods against receipt with pricing calculations to be settled between European governments. The VOC accepted this arrangement and received ammunition supplies on receipt from the French administration.

output.title: Discharge of Captain-Lieutenant Heupner from Armory Oversight
output.abstract: Record of the dismissal of Captain-Lieutenant Klaas Ditloff Heupner from his position as superintendent (opsiender) of the weapons chamber due to advancing age and declining health, while retaining his rank as captain of artillery. The document also references ammunition inventory reconciliation with the French government and matters concerning private trade and commerce.

output.title: Governance Authority and Arrest Powers: Concerns Over Gubernatorial Discretion
output.abstract: This VOC document discusses concerns about the arbitrary exercise of authority by a governor who can arrest officials at will, undermining administrative measures. References Colonel D'Hugonet and tensions between the Dutch Republic and the Emperor. The Fiscal's report to the Zeeland Chamber directors details the arrested official's resistance to government authority, emphasizing the urgency of immediate action to prevent further complications.

output.title: Judicial Proceedings Against Regiment of Luxembourg and Military Discipline Concerns
output.abstract: VOC official report documenting criminal proceedings initiated against the Regiment of Luxembourg and its accomplices, with the fiscal instructed to prosecute according to legal procedure. The document details ongoing conflicts between VOC administration and the Luxembourg regiment, escalating to judicial intervention by the Zeeland chamber. Officials express concern about maintaining military discipline and control over an excessively large military force, warning of dangerous consequences for company interests if the regiment continues operating without proper subordination.

output.title: Luxembourg Regiment Supply and Equipment Provisions under Capitulation
output.abstract: VOC ordinance detailing provisions for the Luxembourg regiment's integration with Company forces. Addresses surplus payment in stuivers, supply of nanking linen and textiles from Company warehouses for uniforms at standard rates equivalent to Dutch military provisions, and issuance of weapons to recruits lacking firearms. Annual accounting procedures established with costs charged to the regiment and submitted to the Zeeland chamber, with the Prince of Luxembourg bearing expenses per Capitulation terms.

output.title: VOC Military Personnel Roster: Soldiers, Musketeers, and Sailors
output.abstract: A detailed muster roll documenting VOC military personnel including soldiers, musketeers (musschieters), sailors (mattroosen), and a drummer. Lists 50+ individuals with their names and places of origin across Europe and VOC territories (Malacca, Nagapatnam, Silhaut). Includes reference to Jaffanese detachment at Tinkonmale with 13 personnel. Represents typical VOC garrison composition combining European recruits with colonial-based forces.
